messages.author: 6d020fc5d7c9ee0a
messages.subject: Spatial Model Compiling Errors
parts:
Dear Stan Group,

I am trying to fit a GP spatial model over T time points (years) where there is spatial dependence within each year, but across years independence is assumed and the spatial parameters do not vary.  Thus, the covariance matrix is block diagonal (D \otimes Identity matrix).  The spatial structure and parameters are the same across years, so I am trying to just have to take the inverse of the covariance matrix once for all T years.  

I have fit the model for individual years in Stan, but when I try and estimate the parameters over all T, I'm getting long source code/compiler errors. I initially tried to separate the T time points using an array for the model matrix, but ran into trouble so I created an ID variable instead for each T.  

Below is my Rstan code, and I can attach the data file if that would be helpful.  The data set is not terribly large (180 observations).  I am wondering if the way I am separating the years is causing the issue, but I am not sure.  Any insight would be much appreciated. 

data{
  int<lower=1> N; //total obs (L*T)
  int<lower=1> L; // total number of locations per year
  int<lower=1> T; //number of years, assume independence across years
  int<lower=1> p; //number of covariates
  int <lower=1> id[N];  // ID By T (year)
  vector [N] Y; // response vector
  matrix[N,p] X;// Model Matrix
  matrix [L,L] d; //distance matrix, same across all years so only need to define once
}

parameters {
  vector[p] beta; # coefficient
  real<lower=0> sigma; # error sd
  real<lower=0> tau; # sd spatial process
  real<lower=0> phi; # range/decay parameter
}


transformed parameters {
  real<lower=0> sigma2;
  real<lower=0> tau2;
  sigma2 = sigma^2;
  tau2 = tau^2;
  
}

model {
  vector[N] mu; 
  matrix[L,L] H; // Same Spatial Parameters for Each Year
  matrix[L,L] Hinv;
  
  for (i in 1:(L-1)) {
    for (j in (i+1):L) {
        H[i,j] = tau2 * exp(-d[i,j]/ phi);
        H[j,i] = H[i,j]; // do not calculate twice, utilize symmetry
      }
    }
  for (k in 1:L) {
    H[k, k] = sigma2 + tau2; //diagonal of covariance matrix
  }
  
  Hinv = inverse_spd(H); //inverse of covariance matrix, should just have to do this once 
  
  
  target += -.5*log_determinant(H); // this step only has to be done once across all years
  
  //calculate the mean for each year using index variable

  for (n in 1:N){
  mu[n] = Y[id[n]] - X[id[n]]*beta;
  }

  
  // increment the likelihood for each T (year)
  for (t in 1:T){
  target += -.5*(mu[id[t]])'*Hinv*(mu[id[t]]);  //MVN is block diagonal so likelihood is incremented by year
  }

  //priors

  //inproper prios on betas.
  sigma ~ cauchy(0,1);
  tau ~ cauchy(0,1);
  phi ~ gamma(0.5,0.5);
}

messages.author: 3d7541308bd2e290
messages.subject: Re: Spatial Model Compiling Errors
parts:
Real quick, is there a reason you're incrementing the log probability manually like this and not using statements like:

y ~ multi_normal(mu, H);

Cause if you can do stuff like that, then you can just do:

L = cholesky_decompose(H);

Followed by a bunch of (with the ys and mus changed to whatever they need to be):

y ~ multi_normal_cholesky(mu, L);

As described in the manual (section 17.4). Computing the Cholesky just once per step should be the speedup you're looking for. Maybe if you can write your model like this it'll be easier to figure out what's going wrong in the model?

Ben

messages.author: 3d7541308bd2e290
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Re: Spatial Model Compiling Errors
parts:
Howdy Colin

Yeah I agree with you. I meant that the 'H' variable would be one of these small blocks.

So if I understand your model correctly, each set of data you model as a Gaussian process with different means but the same covariance.

So:
for (d in 1:D)
    y[d] ~ multi_normal(mu[d], H);

Where 'd' are your days, and H is the small covariance matrix (the same H as in your model, not the covariance matrix for all D days lumped together).

Can't you just write your model like this? There is the issue that at each day you need to have data measured at the same points for them to share the covariance matrix, but if you have that, then you can get the speedup you're looking for by doing:

L = cholesky_decomposition(H)
for (d in 1:D)
    y[d] ~ multi_normal_cholesky(mu[d], L);

It's a Cholesky instead of an inversion cause computing matrix inverses by themselves is a Bad Idea. Solving Ax = b is strongly preferred over trying to compute A^-1 and then multiplying it by b. The Cholesky factorization makes it way easier to do the solves, and so will have the effect you're looking for.

Ben

messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Re: Spatial Model Compiling Errors
parts:
The way I'd do it is arrange y like:

vector[L] Y[T];

So that means you have T vectors of length L (like you have arranged mu in your model block). Then you can just use:

for (t in 1:T)
    y[t] ~ multi_normal_cholesky(mu[t], L);
Ben

messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Spatial Model Compiling Errors
parts:
Hi Bob,

Thanks.  Yes, I would like a varying slope and intercept for each time point, but with a constant covariance matrix.  I think I figured out the way to subset the data correctly and model seems to be running fine now.  See below if anyone else is interested.  



data{

int<lower=1> L; // total number of locations per year
  int<lower=1> T; //number of years, assume independence across years

matrix [L,T] Y; // response vector
  matrix [L,T] X;

matrix [L,L] d; //distance matrix, same across all years
}

parameters {
  real alpha [T]; //intercept
  real beta [T]; //slope

real<lower=0> sigma; # error sd
  real<lower=0> tau; # sd spatial process
  real<lower=0> phi; # range/decay parameter
}


transformed parameters {
  real<lower=0> sigma2;
  real<lower=0> tau2;
  sigma2 = sigma^2;
  tau2 = tau^2;
  
}

model {

matrix[L,L] H; // Same Spatial Paramters for Each Year
   
   for (i in 1:(L-1)) {
     for (j in (i+1):L) {
       H[i,j] = tau2 * exp(-d[i,j]/ phi);
       H[j,i] = H[i,j]; // do not calculate twice, utilize symmetry
     }
   }
   for (k in 1:L) {
     H[k, k] = sigma2 + tau2; //diagonal of covariance matrix
   }

for (i in 1:T){
   Y[,i] ~ multi_normal(alpha[i] + X[,i]*beta[i], H);
}
   
   //priors 
   //inproper priors on coefficients

sigma ~ cauchy(0,1);
   tau ~ cauchy(0,1);
   phi ~ gamma(0.5,0.5);
}

> On May 4, 2017, at 11:14 AM, Colin Lewis-Beck <clewi...@gmail.com> wrote:

> Thanks for the follow up Bob.  That will definitely speed up the code.
>
> One more quick question about subsetting the y and mu vector.   As you can see below, I am sub-setting them by indexing manually.  I know Rstan has a segment function to subset vectors.  However, is there a way to append or add an id variable for each year so I can separate y and mu by year using a loop?

I'm not sure what you're asking in the way of modeling.  Obviously
you can add an ID variable,

  int ID[Y];

but what do you want to do with it?  Do you want a varying intercept
or something?

- Bob

>
> Thanks again,
>
> Colin
>
>  data{
>   int<lower=1> N; //total obs (L*T)
>   int<lower=1> L; // total number of locations per year
>   int<lower=1> T; //number of years, assume independence across years
>   int id [N]; // vector of length N to id Year
>   int<lower=1> p; //number of covariates
>   vector [N] Y; // response vector
>   matrix[N,p] X;// Model Matrix
>   matrix [L,L] d; //distance matrix, same across all years
> }
>
> transformed data{
>   vector [L] Ysub [T];  //break up Y by years T with L obs each Year
>   Ysub[1] = Y[1:30];
>   Ysub[2] = Y[31:60];
>   Ysub[3] = Y[61:90];
>   Ysub[4] = Y[91:120];
>   Ysub[5] = Y[121:150];
>   Ysub[6] = Y[151:180];
> }
>
> parameters {
>   vector[p] beta; # coefficient
>   real<lower=0> sigma; # error sd
>   real<lower=0> tau; # sd spatial process
>   real<lower=0> phi; # range/decay parameter
> }
>
>
> transformed parameters {
>   real<lower=0> sigma2;
>   real<lower=0> tau2;
>   sigma2 = sigma^2;
>   tau2 = tau^2;
>
> }
>
> model {
>    vector [N] mu
>    vector [L] mu_yr[T];  //for Group Means
>    matrix[L,L] H; // Same Spatial Paramters for Each Year
>
>    for (i in 1:(L-1)) {
>      for (j in (i+1):L) {
>        H[i,j] = tau2 * exp(-d[i,j]/ phi);
>        H[j,i] = H[i,j]; // do not calculate twice, utilize symmetry
>      }
>    }
>    for (k in 1:L) {
>      H[k, k] = sigma2 + tau2; //diagonal of covariance matrix
>    }
>
>   mu = X*beta; //overall mean vector
>
>    //seperate by year
>   mu_yr[1] = mu[1:30];
>   mu_yr[2] = mu[31:60];
>   mu_yr[3] = mu[61:90];
>   mu_yr[4] = mu[91:120];
>   mu_yr[5] = mu[121:150];
>   mu_yr[6] = mu[151:180];
>
>
>   Ysub ~ multi_normal(mu_yr, Sigma);
>
>    //priors
>    sigma ~ cauchy(0,1);
>    tau ~ cauchy(0,1);
>    phi ~ gamma(0.5,0.5);
> }
>
> On Thu, May 4, 2017 at 8:48 AM, Bob Carpenter <ca...@alias-i.com> wrote:
> I should've responded to this one.  If you declare
>
>   vector[L] y[T];
>
> then you can just write
>
>   y ~ multi_normal(mu, Sigma);
>
> rather than Cholesky decomposing and the multi_normal will do
> it for you and everything gets vectorized internally.
>
> - Bob
>
> > On May 3, 2017, at 11:52 AM, Ben B <bbba...@gmail.com> wrote:
> >
> > The way I'd do it is arrange y like:
> >
> > vector[L] Y[T];
> >
> > So that means you have T vectors of length L (like you have arranged mu in your model block). Then you can just use:
> >
> > for (t in 1:T)
> >     y[t] ~ multi_normal_cholesky(mu[t], L);
> >
> > Ben
> >

interface lets us mark issues as closed/answered, which should be helpful.

- Bob

> }

> real<lower=0> phi; # range/decay parameter
> }
>

> }
> }
> for (k in 1:L) {
> H[k, k] = sigma2 + tau2; //diagonal of covariance matrix
> }
>
> for (i in 1:T){
> Y[,i] ~ multi_normal(alpha[i] + X[,i]*beta[i], H);

>
> //priors
